newsitem.title: USA: Vanguard says 9-mth inflows top yr ago.
newsitem.headline: Vanguard says 9-mth inflows top yr ago.

text.p: Net cash inflows through September for Vanguard Group, the large mutual fund company, has surpassed totals for the year-ago period, Vanguard said.
Vanguard said that net cash inflow into its mutual funds rose to $30 billion for the first nine months of this year, compared with $17.8 billion for the same period a year ago.
Vanguard, a private firm, said the data includes reinvested dividends. For October, about $2.7 billion flowed into its funds.
The Wall Street Journal reported on Thursday that in the first nine months, Vanguard, based in Valley Forge, Pa., edged past Fidelity Investments in attracting new money.

The newspaper reported that data collected by Strategic Insight attracted 11.2 percent of all net new money going into mutual funds for the first nine months of the year, while Fidelity Investments, of Boston, captured 10.6 percent.
Officials at Strategic Insight did not return telephone calls.
A spokeswoman for Fidelity said the firm doesn't disclose data on net new cash flow into its funds.

The spokeswoman for Fidelity, which is also private, said that it has experienced a slowdown in growth in its share of overall sales of equity funds compared with last year. However, sales "remain quite strong," the spokeswoman said.

A Fidelity source said that the slowdown was likely due to the current popularity of index funds. Fidelity has only one equity index fund, while Vanguard has three equity index funds, plus another six index-related funds.

Fidelity said retirement assets as a percentage of total fund assets will surpass the 1995 total. Through the second quarter of this year, Fidelity has $194.9 billion in retirement assets, out of total fund assets of $415 billion.
For all of 1995, the retirement assets totalled $171.4 billion out of total assets of $373.1 billion.
